atomicSQLAudit.method: Copied actual claim/insert/save/clear SQL from transfer-competition-store.ts, substituted quoteGuard literal, ran it transactionally in native in-memory Python SQLite with current migrations. No source or project database was written.
passedCases: claim commits one row plus matching quote lease
stale claim changes neither row nor lease
duplicate session primary-key insert error rolls back preceding quote lease update
finish commits immutable report and clears matching lease together
stale finish changes neither report nor lease
forced quote-clear SQL error rolls back preceding session-finish update
atomicSQLAudit.limits: Tests support SQLite transaction and SQL predicate reasoning. They are not a separate hosted D1 integration run.

admissionAndCompletionAudit.result: No confirmed blocking defect in the reviewed paths.
evidence: Claim quote update and session insert share one D1 batch. A zero quote CAS prevents the guarded insert; an insertion constraint exception rolls back the update.
Checkpoint and finish re-read actual current files, saved plan, membership, full registration and payment state. Old run identities cannot clear a different current lease.
Replacement, acceptance, checkout, authorization, capture, return, submit and void routes/workflow reject a pending transferCompetitionRun.
Runtime, journey and legacy model admissions include the new lease, with shared readiness and acceptance/payment guards. Legacy definition/digest is preserved.
Completed competing-transfer reports remain supplemental separate-table evidence, not automatic contract acceptance or payment permission.

limitations: Source audit and constructed counterexamples do not prove every interleaving or crash point.
Transformed retained report experiments are not new native execution.
Controlled fetch responses are not a real browser or independently deployed seller.
No competitor implementation was executed by this review; no award probability or full product superiority is inferred.
